The *Kumudamāliyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past karmic deed and subsequent spiritual attainment of the elder (thera) Kumudamāliya, typically featuring an offering of kumuda flowers or garlands to an earlier Buddha or worthy recipient [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali tradition, however, DharmaNexus detects significant internal text reuse, registering 47 matching passages across 13 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive reuse occurs in the first volume of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo; 18 matches, up to 1,400 characters), which aligns directly with §2.3–3.4 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares standard formulaic verses describing devotional flower offerings, karmic fruit, and spiritual liberation with numerous other flower-offering accounts in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Aggapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 262), *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 270 and Tha-Ap 372), *Ticampakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 256), and *Tīṇuppalamāliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 344) [DharmaNexus].
